newsitem.title: USA: Archer says budgeteers closing in on tax numbers.
newsitem.headline: Archer says budgeteers closing in on tax numbers.

text.p: The White House and congressional Republicans are "pretty close on the tax side" as part of a five-year balanced budget deal, House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer said Wednesday.

He told reporters "it would be nice" if budget negotiators agreed on a net $100 billion in tax reduction over a five-year period. He said a tax deal had to accommodate a broad-based capital gains reduction and significant improvement in estate taxes. He called for action on the alternative minimum tax.
Archer said that for budget talks to be successful, "both sides have got to give up something and both sides have got to get something."
White House officials and Republican congressional leaders have been engaged in intense negotiations on a framework of a five-year balanced budget deal.

Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott also said earlier he expected differences with the White House over tax cut proposals could be resolved. "They still want to get more tax increases than we think are achievable. We still would like to have more net tax cuts than have been agreed to. But it's close," Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said.

Republicans have said they want a $100 billion net tax cut over five years while President Clinton in his budget proposed a gross tax cut of $98 billion offset by $76 in tax hikes, for a net tax cut of $22 billion.
